root.label: Attributes
root.note: Annotations on entities and statements: diagnostic requests, hints, and promises the optimizer may exploit.

children.label: Syntax and placement
children.note: Double brackets; the position decides what an attribute appertains to.

children.label: Arguments
children.note: An attribute may take a parenthesized list of balanced tokens, as in deprecated("use g").

children.label: using prefix (C++17)
children.note: [[using gnu: hot, cold]] namespaces a list; the names inside cannot be namespaced again.

children.label: Class attributes
children.note: Write struct [[nodiscard]] S; an attribute before struct with no declarator is ill-formed.

children.label: Statements and labels
children.note: likely, unlikely and fallthrough attach to statements or labels, not declarations.

children.label: Unknown vs misplaced
children.note: Unrecognized attributes are ignored; standard ones used wrongly are errors.

children.label: Ignored (C++17)
children.note: An unrecognized attribute token is ignored; in C++11 and C++14 this was implementation-defined.

children.label: Misplaced standard
children.note: A standard attribute applied where it cannot apply makes the program ill-formed.

children.label: __has_cpp_attribute
children.note: Yields 0 if unsupported, otherwise a date such as 201907L for nodiscard.

children.label: Diagnostic requests
children.note: They encourage warnings and never make code ill-formed by being violated.

children.label: nodiscard
children.note: C++17; reason string and constructors in C++20; type form covers by-value returns only.

children.label: deprecated
children.note: C++14; optional message; works on namespaces, enumerators and specializations.

children.label: maybe_unused
children.note: C++17; silences unused warnings for variables, functions, types and bindings.

children.label: fallthrough
children.note: C++17 null statement; the next statement must carry a case or default label.

children.label: Hints and layout
children.note: Optimization information that compilers may ignore.

children.label: likely, unlikely
children.note: C++20 path probability hints; both on one statement is ill-formed.

children.label: no_unique_address
children.note: C++20; lets a member overlap others, changing sizeof; MSVC ignores it.

children.label: Same-type rule
children.note: Two distinct objects of the same type never share an address.

children.label: Promises
children.note: Breaking these is undefined behavior, and the optimizer relies on them.

children.label: noreturn
children.note: C++11; returning is UB; the first declaration must carry it if any does.

children.label: assume (C++23)
children.note: The expression is not evaluated; if it would be false, behavior is undefined.

children.label: assume vs assert
children.note: assert checks in debug builds; assume never checks and lets code be deleted.

children.label: indeterminate (C++26)
children.note: Opts an uninitialized variable out of erroneous behavior back into UB on read.
